The '''2015–16 Football League Cup''' (known as the '''[[Capital One]] Cup''' for sponsorship purposes) was the 56th season of the [[EFL Cup|Football League Cup]]. It began on 11 August 2015 and concluded on 28 February 2016.<ref name="FASchedule">{{cite web |title=The 2015-16 fixture list has been released by The FA |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2015/may/fa-fixture-list-2015-16-120515 |website=thefa.com |publisher=The FA |date=12 May 2015 |access-date=9 June 2015 }}</ref> It was a knock-out competition for the top 92 [[Association football|football]] clubs played in [[English football league system]].

[[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] were the defending champions, having beaten [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] 2–0 in the [[2015 Football League Cup Final|previous season's final]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/31572594 |title=Chelsea 2–0 Tottenham Hotspur |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |first=Phil |last=McNulty |date=1 March 2015 |access-date=9 June 2015}}</ref> However, they were eliminated in the fourth round by [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] on penalties.

[[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] won the [[2016 Football League Cup Final|final]] on 28 February, defeating [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] 3–1 in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] after the match had finished 1–1 after [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2016/feb/28/liverpool-v-manchester-city-capital-one-cup-final-live|title=Liverpool 1 Man City 1 (Man City win 3-1 on penalties_|date=28 February 2016|work=The Guardian|access-date=8 March 2016}}</ref>

This was the final season in which the tournament was known as the Football League Cup, as it was renamed the EFL Cup in 2016 after the Football League was rebranded as the [[English Football League]] (EFL).<ref>{{cite web|author=Press Association |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/nov/12/goodbye-football-league-hello-english-football-league-rebranding-announced |title=Goodbye Football League, hello English Football League: rebranding announced |work=The Guardian |date=2015-11-12 |access-date=2016-05-30}}</ref>

==Format==
The League Cup was open to all 92 members of the [[Premier League]] and the [[English Football League|Football League]] and was divided into seven rounds, organised so that 32 teams remained by the third round.<ref name="soccerdata">{{cite web |title=The Football League Cup |url=http://www.soccer.mistral.co.uk/books/flctext.htm |work=soccer.mistral.co.uk |publisher=SoccerData |access-date=29 August 2012 |archive-date=5 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181005085103/http://www.soccer.mistral.co.uk/books/flctext.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> Teams involved in European competition during the season received a bye to the third round, the remaining Premier League teams entered at the second round, and the remaining Football League teams entered at the first round.<ref name="soccerdata"/>

The League Cup was played as a [[Single-elimination tournament|knockout cup competition]] for each tie, being played as a single match (with the exception of the semi-finals) with the winner advancing to the next round. The semi-finals were played over [[two-legged tie|two legs]], with each team playing one leg at home, and the teams that scored more goals on aggregate over the two legs advancing to the final. If the score was level after 90 minutes, or if the aggregate score was level for semi-finals, then thirty minutes of [[Overtime (sports)#Association football)|extra time]] were played, divided into two fifteen-minute halves. If the aggregate scores in semi-finals were still level at the end of extra time, the tie was decided by goals scored away from home counting twice, according to the [[away goals rule]]. If the tie was not decided during extra time, it was determined by a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]].<ref name="regulations">{{cite web |title=Rules |url=http://www.capitalonecup.co.uk/competition/rules/ |website=capitalonecup.co.uk |publisher=The Football League |access-date=12 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160314235032/http://www.capitalonecup.co.uk/competition/rules/ |archive-date=2016-03-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In the first five rounds, the team drawn first played at their home ground, and in the semi-finals the team drawn first played the first leg at home. The final was played on a neutral ground.<ref name="regulations" />

==Team allocation==
92 teams from the top four English tiers ([[Premier League]], [[Football League Championship]], [[Football League One]] and [[Football League Two]]) participated.

The tournament was organised so that 32 teams remained by the third round.<ref name="soccerdata"/> Teams involved in European competition received a bye to the third round, the remaining Premier League teams entered at the second round, and the remaining Football League teams entered at the first round.<ref name="soccerdata"/>

==First round==
A total of 72 teams played in the first round: 24 teams from [[Football League Two|League Two]] (tier 4), 24 teams from [[Football League One|League One]] (tier 3), and 24 teams from the [[Football League Championship|Championship]] (tier 2).<ref name="draw1"/> The draw for the first round was held on 16 June 2015.<ref name="draw1results">{{cite web |title=Capital One Cup 2015/16 Round 1 Draw |url=http://www.capitalonecup.co.uk/news/article/capital-one-cup-201516-round-1-draw-2494383.aspx |website=capitalonecup.co.uk |publisher=The Football League |date=16 June 2015 |access-date=12 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150617124706/http://www.capitalonecup.co.uk/news/article/capital-one-cup-201516-round-1-draw-2494383.aspx |archive-date=2015-06-17 |url-status=dead }}</ref> (Note: The numbers in parentheses are the tier for the team during the 2015–16 season.)

==Second round==

A total of 48 teams played in the second round: 12 teams which entered in this round, and the 36 winners of the first round. The 12 teams entering this round were the teams from the [[2015–16 Premier League]] not involved in any European competition.<ref name="draw2" /> The draw for the second round was held on 13 August 2015.<ref name="draw2results">{{cite web |title=Capital One Cup 2015/16 Round 2 Draw |url=http://www.capitalonecup.co.uk/news/article/capital-one-cup-round-2-draw-2617994.aspx |website=capitalonecup.co.uk |publisher=The Football League |date=13 August 2015 |access-date=18 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150816223755/http://www.capitalonecup.co.uk/news/article/capital-one-cup-round-2-draw-2617994.aspx |archive-date=2015-08-16 |url-status=dead }}</ref> (Note: The numbers in parentheses are the tier for the team during the 2015–16 season.)

==Third round==

===Teams===
A total of 32 teams played in the third round: 8 teams which entered in this round, and the 24 winners of the second round. The eight teams entering this round were the teams from the [[2015–16 Premier League]] involved in European competition in the 2015–16 season. There was no seeding in this round. The lowest ranked team in this round was [[Carlisle United F.C.|Carlisle United]], who played in [[Football League Two|League Two]], the fourth division of English football.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/34059004|title=League Cup third-round draw: Tottenham to host rivals Arsenal|date=25 August 2015|work=BBC Sport|access-date=27 August 2015}}</ref>

==Fourth round==

===Teams===
A total of 16 teams played in the fourth round, all winners of the third round. There was no seeding in this round. ==Quarter-finals==

===Teams===
A total of eight teams played in the quarter-finals, all winners of the fourth round. There was no seeding in this round. The draw for the fifth round was held on 28 October after the completion of the fourth round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/34664048|title= Middlesbrough face Everton in quarter-finals|date=28 October 2015|work=BBC Sport|access-date=29 October 2015}}</ref> The lowest ranked teams in this round were Hull City, Middlesbrough and Sheffield Wednesday, who all played in the Championship, the second division of English football.

==Semi-finals==

===Teams===
A total of four teams played in the semi-finals, all winners of the quarter-finals. There was no seeding in this round. The draw for the semi-finals was held on 2 December 2015 and all of the remaining teams were from the Premier League (top tier).<ref name="drawSFresults">{{cite web |title=League Cup semi-final draw: Manchester City to play Everton |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/34989339 |website=www.bbc.com |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 December 2015 |access-date=2 December 2015 }}</ref>

===Matches===
The semi-finals were played over [[two-legged tie|two legs]], with each team playing one leg at home, and the teams that scored more goals on aggregate over the two legs advanced to the final.

==Broadcasting rights==
The live television rights for the competition were held by the subscription channel [[Sky Sports]], who have held rights to the competition since 1996–97 apart from 2001-02 when the short-lived [[ITV Digital]] had exclusive coverage of that season's League Cup competition as part of the original three year TV deal with [[The Football League]].
